scenario.title: Customers charged twice after checkout (reliability rehearsal, not an official contest problem)
scenario.initial_request: Build an AI assistant that drafts apology replies to customers who complain about being charged twice

F-01.statement: crm-tickets.double_charge_tickets_by_week shows 9, 11, 288, 301 double‑charge tickets for weeks 2026‑W35 through W38 with order volumes ~21k each.

F-02.statement: payments-db.duplicate_captures_by_day shows 0,0,118,124 orders_with_2_captures for days 2026-09-07 through 2026-09-10.

F-03.statement: config-audit.gateway_config_changes shows idempotency_key_enforcement turned off on 2026-09-09 by SH-PAY with note temporary latency debugging and no rollback.

F-04.statement: PSP capture attempts log shows 242 duplicate orders (2026-09-09..10) all as gateway timeout retries without idempotency key; earlier period had 0 duplicates despite 238 retries with idempotency key.

CL-01.statement: Build an AI assistant that drafts apology replies to customers who complain about being charged twice

CL-02.statement: On 09-09 we switched idempotency-key enforcement off on the gateway to debug capture latency. It was meant to be temporary. Gateway timeouts and automatic capture retries have always happened at about the same rate; with the key the PSP drops the retried capture. Turning enforcement back on is a one-setting change through the gateway config tool, but payments operations has to confirm it at runtime.

CL-03.statement: Customers are furious about double charges. We just need faster, nicer apology replies.

H-REQUESTER-FRAME.statement: The requester frames the problem as customers receiving duplicate charges and seeks an AI assistant to generate apology replies.

H-IDEMPOTENCY-DISABLED.statement: Payment gateway capture retries are not enforcing idempotency keys, causing the same order to be charged multiple times.

H-DUPLICATE-CAPTURE-REQUESTS.statement: The checkout process inadvertently sends duplicate capture requests to the PSP for a single order.

H-PSP-RETRY-LOGIC.statement: The PSP logs show multiple capture attempts with the same idempotency key due to merchant-side retry on transient failures.

H-FALSE-PERCEPTION.statement: Support tickets reflect customer perception of double charging, but the charge ledger shows only a single capture per order.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The observation shows a sharp rise in support tickets reporting double charges in weeks 2026‑W37 and W38 (288‑301 tickets) compared with earlier weeks (9‑11 tickets), indicating a recent surge in perceived double‑charge incidents.
Duplicate captures appear on days with high gateway timeout retries, indicating that retries may be causing duplicate charges.

The gateway configuration audit shows that on 2026-09-09 SH-PAY disabled idempotency_key_enforcement (temporary latency debugging) with no rollback, which permits duplicate captures when retries occur.

The observation shows that during 2026-09-09..10, 242 duplicate orders occurred, all as gateway timeout retries sent without idempotency keys, while the earlier period (2026-09-01..08) had zero duplicates despite many retries that were deduplicated and sent with idempotency keys.

E-05.content: On 09-09 we switched idempotency-key enforcement off on the gateway to debug capture latency. It was meant to be temporary. Gateway timeouts and automatic capture retries have always happened at about the same rate; with the key the PSP drops the retried capture. Turning enforcement back on is a one-setting change through the gateway config tool, but payments operations has to confirm it at runtime.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder confirms that idempotency key enforcement was turned off on 2026-09-09 for latency debugging, intended as a temporary change. This timing coincides with the onset of duplicate charge incidents, suggesting the disabled setting allowed retries to cause duplicate captures.

E-06.content: Customers are furious about double charges. We just need faster, nicer apology replies.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder (E-06) reports that customers are furious about perceived double charges and requests faster, nicer apology replies, indicating a communication need but not informing about the root cause of duplicate charges.

E-07.content: Payments change runbook §4: the gateway operation set_capture_idempotency on gateway-config may be executed by automation only after the payments operations manager SH-OPS confirms it at runtime. The change is reversible (setting can be switched back).

interpretation_history.interpretation: The runbook states that the gateway operation set_capture_idempotency can be run by automation only after the payments operations manager (SH-OPS) confirms it at runtime, and the change is reversible.

symptoms: Duplicate charge reports in support tickets
problem_definition.root_problem: If idempotency key enforcement is disabled on the payment gateway, then gateway timeout retries will be processed as duplicate captures, causing duplicate charges.

decision_log.rationale: causal chain: Idempotency key enforcement disabled (config change) → Gateway experiences timeout on capture attempt → Gateway automatically retries capture without idempotency key (enforcement off) → PSP processes retry as a new capture (no deduplication) → Order receives two captures → duplicate charge observed; rejected framings: [('H-DUPLICATE-CAPTURE-REQUESTS', 'Contradicted by evidence E-04 showing duplicate orders originate from gateway timeout retries, not duplicate capture requests from checkout.'), ('H-FALSE-PERCEPTION', 'Contradicted by evidence E-02, E-03, E-04 confirming actual duplicate captures, not merely perception.'), ('H-PSP-RETRY-LOGIC', 'Contradicted by evidence E-04 showing PSP logs have zero duplicates from other paths and all duplicates lack idempotency keys.'), ('H-REQUESTER-FRAME', "While supported by evidence, the requester's framing (AI assistant for apology replies) addresses symptom, not root cause; adopting it would not prevent duplicate charges.")]
